brief.title: AI 工程简报：MCP 权限控制、Agent 评测与工具调用训练
brief.overview: 过去 24 小时抓取覆盖：OpenAI 首次连接超时、重试后无条目；Hugging Face、Google 无 24 小时内更新；TechCrunch 仅有企业股权与人事变动类消息，与你的工程关注点不符（且涉及融资类内容已排除）。以下 5 条均来自 arXiv 本次抓取，聚焦 Agent、工具调用与 AI 编程；论文结论均保留其模型规模、任务与实验条件，不等同于生产结论。

items.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
items.summary: 论文提出 Structured Authority Injection（SAI）：把操作者的纠正指令通过带类型、经 schema 校验的 MCP 工具调用注入，并在每次提示前附加排序后的“权威上下文”。它定义 Constraint、Priority、Strategy 三类覆盖及明确优先级，由规划进程无法访问的定向通道执行；无需微调或访问模型权重，适用于支持 MCP 工具调用的指令微调模型。在 9 个 LLM、8 个针对 Agent 失效模式的场景中，作者报告歧义指令解释减少、跨规划轮次的指令权威衰减得到缓解，最强模型提示开销最多降低 38%，但收益随模型和场景差异较大。
items.why_it_matters: 你在设计后端 Agent 的 MCP 工具层时，通常只有参数校验，缺少“人类指令优先级”这一层。该文的 typed override、独立优先级通道和三类语义，可作为权限与约束模型的参考；但收益模型依赖明显，不宜直接当作默认架构。

items.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
items.summary: Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）是一套评测协议，把自动优化提示、工具、技能与编排代码带来的“harness 进化”增益拆成三部分：基准过拟合、测试时算力扩展带来的提升、以及可能泛化的剩余增益。作者在 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 进化框架以及数学、编程、创意和 Agent 任务上评估：在 21 个搜索集增益显著的设置中，过拟合平均占 54%、测试时扩展占 14%，两者合计在 14 个设置中超过 50%。搜索集增益经常无法迁移到留出任务，验证集信号也不足以防止过拟合。
items.why_it_matters: 如果你用自动搜索或迭代调参来提升 Agent 的提示、工具和编排，这套拆分方法能避免把过拟合和“多花推理算力”误当成真实能力提升；建议内部评测保留留出任务，并记录同等算力基线。

items.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
items.summary: Lean4AgenticRL 用统一的 Lean4 形式化为开放式 Agent 强化学习提供多级过程奖励，覆盖底层工具调用、中层工作流阶段和高层结果，并配合按工作流阶段归一化的 GRPO 训练。作者用它训练 LAR-9B/27B：LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%，模型平均比基座高 9.89%，比已知同规模第二名高 5.07%。实验集中在软件工程和终端使用任务；摘要未说明 LAR 系列权重是否公开。
items.why_it_matters: 工具调用级奖励正是自建 SWE/终端 Agent 训练时最难设计的一环；其“工作流阶段 + 工具调用”奖励拆分和归一化 GRPO 值得复现实验。若你关注开源模型，需注意论文目前只报告训练结果，未提权重发布。

items.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
items.summary: 作者用隐藏的 PDDL 形式语义检验 LLM Agent 的规划能力：每个任务都有可判定动作是否适用、目标是否达成、计划是否存在的模型。实验覆盖 5 个领域、4 个模型、6 种提示策略和 3 种 Agent 架构。最佳配置在离线条件下解决 78% 可解任务，在线执行时只有 40%，多数情况下 Agent 未检查状态就行动；不可解任务识别率低于 10%；更重的提示策略消耗 5 至 22 倍 token，却没有明显收益。性能差异更多来自模型，而非提示策略或架构。
items.why_it_matters: 这直接质疑“端到端成功率”和 LLM 评审对 Agent 规划能力的证明力。你搭工具调用循环时，应记录并校验动作轨迹与状态变化，而不是仅靠堆叠反思、搜索等提示策略。

items.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
items.summary: PRIME 要求 Agent 在检查前先固定“证据路线”，明确每种结论需要哪些检查来授权；由独立程序记录每次检查结果，并拒绝结果无法支撑的结论，还会指出可支持更强结论的检查或自行执行。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接看到需求的 Agent 有 26.7% 的任务给出未经证明的结论，PRIME 报告为零；在“只允许拒绝”时平均得分 30.1（满分 59.2），加入其指引和补充检查后达到满分。该保证依赖需求正确、检查位置已知且预算充足。
items.why_it_matters: 漏洞报告、合规审查这类后端流程，可把“结论必须由检查账本授权”实现为独立校验服务，而不是信任模型自述。该设计适合工具调用结果的硬性把关，但前提是需求规则和检查点本身可靠。

{"id": "da92b80397690dde35e8", "title": "Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22373", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22373 (cs) [Submitted on 27 Jul 2026] Title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides Authors: Ryan Tran , YueMing Zhang , Lingfeng Tao , Nan Yang , Shengjie Xu , Yu Yin , Shuai Xu , Wenlu Zhang , Hailu Xu View a PDF of the paper titled Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides, by Ryan Tran and 8 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control. {"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22466 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution Authors: Wenxuan Ding , Qin Lu , Changlong Yu , Sha Li , Shuowei Jin , Xin Liu , Zhenyu Shi , Greg Durrett View a PDF of the paper titled Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution, by Wenxuan Ding and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research. {"id": "a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba", "title": "Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22448", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Machine Learning arXiv:2610.22448 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards Authors: Ruida Wang , Gerald Friedland , Tong Zhang , Chris Kong View a PDF of the paper titled Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards, by Ruida Wang and 3 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL. {"id": "8cad1d7071d358947cb2", "title": "Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22469", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22469 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics Authors: Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu , Oscar Miró López-Feliu , Victor Gimenez-Abalos , Javier Vazquez-Salceda , Victor Carballo Araruna , Sergio Alvarez-Napagao View a PDF of the paper titled Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics, by Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces. {"id": "434246a93fec15537b14", "title": "PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22426", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22426 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents Authors: Hamed Khosravi , Xiaoming Huo View a PDF of the paper titled PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents, by Hamed Khosravi and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100. article_id='a97c1f5a709e4de6f7ba' summary='Lean4AgenticRL 用统一的 Lean4 形式化为开放式 Agent 强化学习提供多级过程奖励，覆盖底层工具调用、中层工作流阶段和高层结果，并配合按工作流阶段归一化的 GRPO 训练。作者用它训练 LAR-9B/27B：LAR-27B 在 TerminalBench-2.1 上达到 77.3%，模型平均比基座高 9.89%，比已知同规模第二名高 5.07%。实验集中在软件工程和终端使用任务；摘要未说明 LAR 系列权重是否公开。' why_it_matters='工具调用级奖励正是自建 SWE/终端 Agent 训练时最难设计的一环；其“工作流阶段 + 工具调用”奖励拆分和归一化 GRPO 值得复现实验。若你关注开源模型，需注意论文目前只报告训练结果，未提权重发布。' topic='Agent 训练 / 开源模型' relevance=3

article_id='8cad1d7071d358947cb2' summary='作者用隐藏的 PDDL 形式语义检验 LLM Agent 的规划能力：每个任务都有可判定动作是否适用、目标是否达成、计划是否存在的模型。实验覆盖 5 个领域、4 个模型、6 种提示策略和 3 种 Agent 架构。最佳配置在离线条件下解决 78% 可解任务，在线执行时只有 40%，多数情况下 Agent 未检查状态就行动；不可解任务识别率低于 10%；更重的提示策略消耗 5 至 22 倍 token，却没有明显收益。性能差异更多来自模型，而非提示策略或架构。' why_it_matters='这直接质疑“端到端成功率”和 LLM 评审对 Agent 规划能力的证明力。你搭工具调用循环时，应记录并校验动作轨迹与状态变化，而不是仅靠堆叠反思、搜索等提示策略。' topic='Agent 规划与评测' relevance=2

article_id='434246a93fec15537b14' summary='PRIME 要求 Agent 在检查前先固定“证据路线”，明确每种结论需要哪些检查来授权；由独立程序记录每次检查结果，并拒绝结果无法支撑的结论，还会指出可支持更强结论的检查或自行执行。在 480 个公共记录任务上，直接看到需求的 Agent 有 26.7% 的任务给出未经证明的结论，PRIME 报告为零；在“只允许拒绝”时平均得分 30.1（满分 59.2），加入其指引和补充检查后达到满分。该保证依赖需求正确、检查位置已知且预算充足。' why_it_matters='漏洞报告、合规审查这类后端流程，可把“结论必须由检查账本授权”实现为独立校验服务，而不是信任模型自述。该设计适合工具调用结果的硬性把关，但前提是需求规则和检查点本身可靠。' topic='Agent 可靠性 / 工具调用校验' relevance=2

selected_evidence.title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22426 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents Authors: Hamed Khosravi , Xiaoming Huo View a PDF of the paper titled PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents, by Hamed Khosravi and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100. selected_evidence.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22469 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics Authors: Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu , Oscar Miró López-Feliu , Victor Gimenez-Abalos , Javier Vazquez-Salceda , Victor Carballo Araruna , Sergio Alvarez-Napagao View a PDF of the paper titled Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics, by Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces. selected_evidence.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Machine Learning arXiv:2610.22448 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards Authors: Ruida Wang , Gerald Friedland , Tong Zhang , Chris Kong View a PDF of the paper titled Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards, by Ruida Wang and 3 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL. selected_evidence.title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22373 (cs) [Submitted on 27 Jul 2026] Title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides Authors: Ryan Tran , YueMing Zhang , Lingfeng Tao , Nan Yang , Shengjie Xu , Yu Yin , Shuai Xu , Wenlu Zhang , Hailu Xu View a PDF of the paper titled Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides, by Ryan Tran and 8 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control. selected_evidence.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22466 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution Authors: Wenxuan Ding , Qin Lu , Changlong Yu , Sha Li , Shuowei Jin , Xin Liu , Zhenyu Shi , Greg Durrett View a PDF of the paper titled Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution, by Wenxuan Ding and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research. items.summary: WebMix 用混合超网络让 Web Agent 适配未见过的网站界面：先在一批源界面上训练低秩适配器库，部署时由 scout agent 探索目标站点并把观察整理成一份简短说明书，轻量路由器据说明书预测各适配器的混合系数，合成一个新适配器用于推理，目标站点上不做梯度更新。作者用 Qwen 与 Llama 两个模型在 TimeWarp、WebArena-Lite-v2 上评估域迁移、在 TimeWarp 上评估版本迁移，三种设置下均与上下文学习及 LoRA 基线持平或更优，TimeWarp 域迁移平均约高 8 个百分点；在已见界面上未出现退化。
items.why_it_matters: 你维护的后端 Agent 若依赖网页/控制台操作，站点改版常导致脚本与选择器失效。该方案把“适配新界面”变成一次探索加一次前向计算，而不是每个站点重训，可作为工具层抽象与降级路径的参考；但它评估的是浏览器任务成功率，接入内网系统仍需自行验证。

items.title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis
items.summary: 论文关注 LLM 作为“形式化器”时的隐性错误：生成的 SMT-LIB2、MiniZinc、PDDL 规格能跑通但语义有误（约束、域、目标或谓词写错），而求解器一旦不再报错就失去反馈；纯 LLM 自评诊断在其实验中会让 11.8% 原本正确的规格变坏。DRAGO 改用与具体形式化语言绑定的确定性诊断，并只在无参考验收谓词下“诊断错误权重严格下降”时才保留改写。跨 5 个基准，回归率降至 1.3%，平均答案准确率比零样本形式化高 12.9 个百分点、比 LLM 诊断修复高 8.7 个百分点；另发现 Planetarium 两个渲染缺陷致其 50%（3,086 例）floor-tile 切分与参考形式化不一致，并发布了修正版切分。
items.why_it_matters: 你若让模型生成配置、策略或校验规则，风险正是“语法合法但语义错误”。该文的“确定性诊断 + 严格接受谓词”可直接映射为后端 CI 中的 schema/约束检查与自动改写门禁，避免模型自评带来的回归；代价是需要为每种目标语言实现诊断器。

items.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: 面向长程 GUI Agent，ECHOES 指出保留历史截图会推高视觉 token 与推理成本，而纯文本摘要会丢失关键状态。方法采用 Compression-Think-Action 格式递归更新文本历史状态；同一模型在多图特权输入下充当教师，对学生自己生成的轨迹做逐 token 的 on-policy 蒸馏，并用 Perception-Memory Fidelity Gap 引导的 OPD-RL 在蒸馏与任务奖励间动态权衡，教师定期更新。作者另构建基于真实失败轨迹的 ECHOESBMK，在 4 个 GUI 基准与 ECHOESBMK 上报告任务表现与记忆保真度提升；部署时不保留历史截图仍具竞争力，并对未见视觉规划任务有正向零样本迁移。
items.why_it_matters: 你的 Agent 若把每轮工具结果全量塞进上下文，成本和长程一致性都会恶化。这里“可递归更新的结构化状态 + 训练期特权信息”的思路，可类比为后端把状态落到持久化存储、只把关键摘要回填 prompt；但该收益来自特定训练流程，纯提示工程无法直接复现。

items.title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
items.summary: 作者把“作者声明”变成 Agent 复现审查的显式输入：结构化清单记录复现步骤与已知限制，GitHub 上两阶段流程把 Agent 检查与作者澄清、修订、再评估串起来；Agent 分别判断“结果是否已复现”和“作者是否需要补充或修复”，人工评审负责批准请求与判定问题是否关闭。系统在 36 篇会议论文、133 个实验表格与图上部署，人工复核后提出 20 个问题，后续检查支持全部关闭，但部分情况完整复现仍未验证；作者还用完整清单与空白清单对照，观察声明如何影响 Agent 的调查与结论。
items.why_it_matters: 这相当于把你的代码审查/回归验证流程产品化：Agent 产出结论、独立记录证据、人类保留裁决权。若你正搭内部 Agent 做构建排障或安全巡检，可借鉴其“声明—检查—澄清—复核”状态机与 GitHub 集成方式；注意论文明确承认部分复现未被验证，不能把“问题已关闭”当作复现成功。

items.title: Predicting Privileged Information Effectiveness for On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: 论文系统研究 on-policy self-distillation 中“特权信息”（PI）该怎么构造：在 3 个多轮 Agent 基准、3 个规模与推理模式不同的学生模型上比较 16 种 PI 配置。结果显示 PI 效果取决于内容、生成来源与学生模型——信息密度高的轨迹、由更强模型生成的 PI 通常收益更大，而 thinking 模型收益不稳定。作者用采样 token 反向 KL 与 error-step KL 对比两个指标在训练前预测 PI 效果，发现它们比易被信息泄漏扭曲的 PI utility 更一致；按 error-step KL 对比逐任务挑选 PI 优于随机选择，PI 与 GRPO 结合时整体目标也优于强 GRPO 基线。
items.why_it_matters: 如果你在做 Agent 轨迹数据的自蒸馏或 RL 微调，这条给出可操作的选数信号：不要只看数据“看起来有用”，而要在训练前用 KL 类指标筛 PI。不过实验限于多轮 Agent 基准与三个学生模型，换到你的工具集与领域仍需重新校准。

WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining. arguments.overview: 覆盖情况（2026-10-18 05:41 至 2026-10-19 05:41 UTC）：OpenAI、Hugging Face、Google 三个源在 24 小时窗口内均返回 0 条；TechCrunch 仅 2 条，分别为 Anthropic 承诺将 5% 股份投入公益基金、Disney 同意接收 Character.AI 大部分员工，属股权与人事交易（融资类已按你偏好排除），未选。arXiv 返回 40 条新论文，其中 5 篇（SAI/MCP 权限、Harness-Delta 归因、Lean4AgenticRL、Agent 规划形式语义检验、PRIME 证据校验）上一期已推送，本轮已剔除。以下 5 条均为本次实际抓取、且未在历史中出现的论文，聚焦 Agent 适配、AI 编程中的规格生成与校验、GUI Agent 成本控制及 Agent 训练；结论均保留其模型、基准与实验条件，不等同于生产可用性结论。
selections: article_id='6ec636eceffcfb5999d5' summary='WebMix 用混合超网络让 Web Agent 适配未见过的网站界面：先在一批源界面上训练低秩适配器库，部署时由 scout agent 探索目标站点并把观察整理成一份简短说明书，轻量路由器据说明书预测各适配器的混合系数，合成一个新适配器用于推理，目标站点上不做梯度更新。作者用 Qwen 与 Llama 两个模型在 TimeWarp、WebArena-Lite-v2 上评估域迁移、在 TimeWarp 上评估版本迁移，三种设置下均与上下文学习及 LoRA 基线持平或更优，TimeWarp 域迁移平均约高 8 个百分点；在已见界面上未出现退化。' why_it_matters='你维护的后端 Agent 若依赖网页/控制台操作，站点改版常导致脚本与选择器失效。该方案把“适配新界面”变成一次探索加一次前向计算，而不是每个站点重训，可作为工具层抽象与降级路径的参考；但它评估的是浏览器任务成功率，接入内网系统仍需自行验证。' topic='Agent / Web 界面适配' relevance=3

article_id='bf13a92368f50af68cba' summary='论文关注 LLM 作为“形式化器”时的隐性错误：生成的 SMT-LIB2、MiniZinc、PDDL 规格能跑通但语义有误（约束、域、目标或谓词写错），而求解器一旦不再报错就失去反馈；纯 LLM 自评诊断在其实验中会让 11.8% 原本正确的规格变坏。DRAGO 改用与具体形式化语言绑定的确定性诊断，并只在无参考验收谓词下“诊断错误权重严格下降”时才保留改写。跨 5 个基准，回归率降至 1.3%，平均答案准确率比零样本形式化高 12.9 个百分点、比 LLM 诊断修复高 8.7 个百分点；另发现 Planetarium 两个渲染缺陷致其 50%（3,086 例）floor-tile 切分与参考形式化不一致，并发布了修正版切分。' why_it_matters='你若让模型生成配置、策略或校验规则，风险正是“语法合法但语义错误”。该文的“确定性诊断 + 严格接受谓词”可直接映射为后端 CI 中的 schema/约束检查与自动改写门禁，避免模型自评带来的回归；代价是需要为每种目标语言实现诊断器。' topic='AI 编程 / 规格生成与校验' relevance=3

article_id='9f9467f75484ebfa07d2' summary='面向长程 GUI Agent，ECHOES 指出保留历史截图会推高视觉 token 与推理成本，而纯文本摘要会丢失关键状态。方法采用 Compression-Think-Action 格式递归更新文本历史状态；同一模型在多图特权输入下充当教师，对学生自己生成的轨迹做逐 token 的 on-policy 蒸馏，并用 Perception-Memory Fidelity Gap 引导的 OPD-RL 在蒸馏与任务奖励间动态权衡，教师定期更新。作者另构建基于真实失败轨迹的 ECHOESBMK，在 4 个 GUI 基准与 ECHOESBMK 上报告任务表现与记忆保真度提升；部署时不保留历史截图仍具竞争力，并对未见视觉规划任务有正向零样本迁移。' why_it_matters='你的 Agent 若把每轮工具结果全量塞进上下文，成本和长程一致性都会恶化。这里“可递归更新的结构化状态 + 训练期特权信息”的思路，可类比为后端把状态落到持久化存储、只把关键摘要回填 prompt；但该收益来自特定训练流程，纯提示工程无法直接复现。' topic='Agent / GUI 长程记忆' relevance=2

article_id='7cc78127c883714f76f3' summary='作者把“作者声明”变成 Agent 复现审查的显式输入：结构化清单记录复现步骤与已知限制，GitHub 上两阶段流程把 Agent 检查与作者澄清、修订、再评估串起来；Agent 分别判断“结果是否已复现”和“作者是否需要补充或修复”，人工评审负责批准请求与判定问题是否关闭。系统在 36 篇会议论文、133 个实验表格与图上部署，人工复核后提出 20 个问题，后续检查支持全部关闭，但部分情况完整复现仍未验证；作者还用完整清单与空白清单对照，观察声明如何影响 Agent 的调查与结论。' why_it_matters='这相当于把你的代码审查/回归验证流程产品化：Agent 产出结论、独立记录证据、人类保留裁决权。若你正搭内部 Agent 做构建排障或安全巡检，可借鉴其“声明—检查—澄清—复核”状态机与 GitHub 集成方式；注意论文明确承认部分复现未被验证，不能把“问题已关闭”当作复现成功。' topic='Agent 工作流 / 工程审查' relevance=2

article_id='1cf7caf1e3962092517f' summary='论文系统研究 on-policy self-distillation 中“特权信息”（PI）该怎么构造：在 3 个多轮 Agent 基准、3 个规模与推理模式不同的学生模型上比较 16 种 PI 配置。结果显示 PI 效果取决于内容、生成来源与学生模型——信息密度高的轨迹、由更强模型生成的 PI 通常收益更大，而 thinking 模型收益不稳定。作者用采样 token 反向 KL 与 error-step KL 对比两个指标在训练前预测 PI 效果，发现它们比易被信息泄漏扭曲的 PI utility 更一致；按 error-step KL 对比逐任务挑选 PI 优于随机选择，PI 与 GRPO 结合时整体目标也优于强 GRPO 基线。' why_it_matters='如果你在做 Agent 轨迹数据的自蒸馏或 RL 微调，这条给出可操作的选数信号：不要只看数据“看起来有用”，而要在训练前用 KL 类指标筛 PI。不过实验限于多轮 Agent 基准与三个学生模型，换到你的工具集与领域仍需重新校准。' topic='Agent 训练 / 自蒸馏' relevance=2

selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Machine Learning arXiv:2610.22539 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks Authors: Md Farhan Ishmam , Minh Pham Dinh , Kenneth Marino View a PDF of the paper titled Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks, by Md Farhan Ishmam and 2 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining. selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22568 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis Authors: Giovanni Vaccarino , Emanuele La Malfa , Dehai Min , Hanrong Zhang , Pier Luca Lanzi , Lu Cheng , Michael J. Wooldridge , Philip S. Yu , Sara Bernardini View a PDF of the paper titled Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis, by Giovanni Vaccarino and 8 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference-free acceptance predicate. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning (SMT-LIB2), constraint programming (MiniZinc), and planning (PDDL), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization and 8.7 percentage points over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% (3,086 instances) of its floor-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split. brief.title: 研究简报：评测方法学三则（2026-10-19）
brief.overview: 过去 24 小时可获取内容中，仅 arXiv cs.AI/cs.LG 有新条目（40 篇）；OpenAI、Google AI、Hugging Face 三个源在本窗口内返回空，TechCrunch 未取用（偏融资/产品，与排除项和主题不符）。按“研究论文 / 模型评测 / benchmark、evaluation”偏好筛出 3 篇，均聚焦评测效度而非新模型发布：一篇把 agent harness 的收益拆解为过拟合、测试时算力与可泛化残差；一篇用形式化语义检验“LLM agent 会规划”的说法；一篇指出推理模型在日常（非形式）逻辑上与普通模型相比并不占优。

items.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
items.summary: 论文提出 Harness-Delta Attribution（HDA）评测协议，把 harness 演化（优化 prompt、工具、编排代码而冻结权重）在搜索集上的增益拆为三部分：基准特定过拟合、测试时算力扩展带来的收益、以及剩余可泛化残差的上界。在 11 个执行模型、3 个 harness 演化框架、覆盖数学/代码/创造力/agent 任务的 21 个出现显著搜索集增益的设置上，过拟合与测试时扩展平均分别解释 54% 与 14%，二者合计在 14 个设置中超过 50%；搜索集增益常无法迁移到留出任务，且仅靠验证集信号不足以阻止过拟合。
items.why_it_matters: 你的研究方向是评测，这类“增益归因”协议可直接用于审阅 agent harness 论文中的 SOTA 数字：以后读到“某框架提升 X%”，可先问其中多少来自过拟合与推理算力，而非方法本身。

items.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
items.summary: 论文用隐藏的 PDDL 形式模型检验 LLM agent 的规划主张：任务以自然语言提出，但由形式语义判定每步动作是否可应用、目标是否达成、是否存在解。覆盖 5 个领域（含 2 个新领域，均随论文发布）、4 个模型、6 种提示策略、3 种 agent 架构。最佳配置离线解出 78% 的可解任务，在线仅 40%；不可解任务仅在不到 10% 的回合中被识别；更重的提示策略消耗 5–22 倍 token 而无明显收益；性能在模型间的差异大于提示策略与架构之间的差异。
items.why_it_matters: 给你一个可复用的评测视角：端到端成功率与 LLM 裁判无法验证过程有效性，若你在做 agent 基准或评审相关论文，动作轨迹的形式化校验是更有说服力的证据。

items.title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
items.summary: 论文构建基于语言与语用推理现象的新基准，系统比较大型推理模型（LRM）与非推理模型在日常逻辑推理上的表现，并控制提示条件。结果显示：当日常推理偏离形式逻辑规则时，推理模型表现常出现下降；部分非推理模型配合 chain-of-thought 提示可超过同级别推理模型；额外指令提示对推理行为的控制有限。作者据此指出当前后训练目标对日常推理的覆盖不足。
items.why_it_matters: 如果你关注推理模型的评测结论是否被数学/科学基准夸大，这篇提供了“形式逻辑之外的推理”这一维度的对照证据，也可作为新基准素材。

{"id": "f34ad45741b405ff9e69", "title": "Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22466 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution Authors: Wenxuan Ding , Qin Lu , Changlong Yu , Sha Li , Shuowei Jin , Xin Liu , Zhenyu Shi , Greg Durrett View a PDF of the paper titled Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution, by Wenxuan Ding and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research. {"id": "8cad1d7071d358947cb2", "title": "Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22469", "source_id": "arxiv", "source": "arXiv cs.AI / cs.LG", "published_at": "2026-10-19T04:00:00+00:00", "text": "Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22469 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics Authors: Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu , Oscar Miró López-Feliu , Victor Gimenez-Abalos , Javier Vazquez-Salceda , Victor Carballo Araruna , Sergio Alvarez-Napagao View a PDF of the paper titled Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics, by Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces. selected_evidence.title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22469 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics Authors: Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu , Oscar Miró López-Feliu , Victor Gimenez-Abalos , Javier Vazquez-Salceda , Victor Carballo Araruna , Sergio Alvarez-Napagao View a PDF of the paper titled Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics, by Oriol Miro-Lopez-Feliu and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces. selected_evidence.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
selected_evidence.text: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence arXiv:2610.22466 (cs) [Submitted on 15 Oct 2026] Title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution Authors: Wenxuan Ding , Qin Lu , Changlong Yu , Sha Li , Shuowei Jin , Xin Liu , Zhenyu Shi , Greg Durrett View a PDF of the paper titled Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution, by Wenxuan Ding and 7 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.
